definitions.explanation: A sea creature with a flat body and usually five arms, found on rocky shores and the sea floor. Written in katakana, or {海星|ひとで} in kanji.

examples.japanese: ⟦{岩|いわ}→岩：00850_iwa⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ヒトデがいた。
examples.english: There was a starfish on the rock.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}ども⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{浜辺|はまべ}→浜辺：17948_hamabe⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧ヒトデ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{拾|ひろ}った→拾う：00845_hirou⟧。
examples.english: The child picked up a starfish on the beach.

examples.japanese: ヒトデ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{腕|うで}→腕：01006_ude⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{一本|いっぽん}→一本：08888_ippon⟧⟦{切|き}れて→切れる：01936_kireru⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧、⟦また→また：00969_mata⟧⟦{生|は}えて→生える：02392_haeru⟧くること⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: A starfish can sometimes grow back an arm that has been cut off.

notes:
The name is said to come from ⟦{人手|ひとで}→人手：25438_hitode⟧ (a human hand), from the shape. Katakana also keeps it apart from ⟦{人出|ひとで}→人出：32354_hitode⟧ (crowds) and ⟦{人手|ひとで}→人手：25438_hitode⟧ (manpower), which share the reading.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ヒトデ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{腕|うで}→腕：01006_ude⟧: a starfish's arm
- ヒトデ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{拾|ひろ}う→拾う：00845_hirou⟧: to pick up a starfish

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ナマコ: sea cucumber — another echinoderm of the shore
